name: Working at Heights
audience: Construction and maintenance workers who work at height
Site staff who use scaffolds, ladders and elevating work platforms
New employees starting in roles that involve working at height
Supervisors who need to understand fall protection for their teams

faqs.q: How much does the Working at Heights course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R700 per person and runs for one day. Group bookings are negotiable, so ask for a quote if you are training a full team. Classes run daily at our Midrand and Durban centres, or we can train on site at your premises. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za to book or to get a group price.

faqs.q: Do I need a medical before working at heights training?
faqs.a: A working at heights medical is mandatory for employees who work at height, and REH Medicals does these. Bring confirmation of your medical fitness when you attend, or ask us about arranging one before your course date. The training itself covers hazard identification, fall protection equipment and safe work practices at height.

faqs.q: How long is the Working at Heights certificate valid?
faqs.a: Your certificate is issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable. Many employers and client sites set their own refresher intervals, so check what your site requires. If you are unsure whether your certificate is still accepted, send it to us via email at info@rehtraining.co.za and we will confirm.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site in Johannesburg?
faqs.a: Yes. We train at client premises across South Africa, and we also run daily classes at our centres in Midrand and Durban. On-site training suits teams of five or more and lets you practise on your own equipment and working conditions. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za or call 010 746 6954 to arrange a date.

name: Fall Arrest Techniques
audience: Workers who use fall arrest systems while working at height
Construction, maintenance and industrial staff who work at height
Safety representatives who check fall protection equipment
New employees who will wear full body harnesses at work

faqs.q: How much does Fall Arrest Techniques training cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R700 per person and runs for one day. It is aligned to SAQA unit standard 229998 at NQF Level 1. Group bookings are negotiable, and daily classes run at our Midrand and Durban centres or on site at your premises. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za to book your seats.

faqs.q: What equipment will I learn to use?
faqs.a: You will practise fitting and using a full body harness, connecting to anchorage points and checking lanyards, connectors and other fall arrest components. The course also covers inspection of equipment, spotting defects and correct storage so your gear stays safe between jobs. You get a certificate on completion, issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable.

faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do this course?
faqs.a: No prior experience is required. The course starts with the basics of fall protection, hazard identification and risk assessment, then builds up to fitting and using the equipment. It suits new employees and experienced workers who want formal certification for working at height. Classes run daily, and you can book at a centre or on site.

faqs.q: How long is the certificate valid?
faqs.a: The certificate is issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable. Employers and client sites often set their own refresher periods for fall protection work, so check what your site requires. If you are not sure your certificate is still current, email us at info@rehtraining.co.za and we will advise you.

name: Fall Arrest Rescue
audience: Rescue team members responsible for responding to fall incidents
Safety officers and supervisors who coordinate emergency response
Workers on sites where fall arrest systems are in use
Employees who may need to rescue a suspended casualty

faqs.q: How much does Fall Arrest Rescue training cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R3500 per person and runs over four days. It is aligned to SAQA unit standard 229995 at NQF Level 3. Daily classes are available at our Midrand and Durban centres, and we can run the course on site for your rescue team. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za for dates and group pricing.

faqs.q: What does the four day course cover?
faqs.a: You learn rescue planning, hazard identification and the correct use of fall rescue equipment. The practical work covers casualty recovery, controlled descent techniques and how to respond to suspension trauma after a fall. The course also covers communication and coordination during a rescue, and post rescue actions. By the end you can take part in organised fall rescue operations.

faqs.q: Do I need experience to do Fall Arrest Rescue?
faqs.a: Some experience of working at height is useful, because the course builds on fall protection knowledge and moves quickly into rescue techniques. If you are new to height work, consider doing the Working at Heights or Fall Arrest Techniques course first. The rescue course suits members of site rescue teams and safety staff who respond to incidents.

faqs.q: Can you train our rescue team at our site?
faqs.a: Yes. On-site training works well for rescue teams because you can practise on your own structures and equipment. We also run daily classes at our centres in Midrand and Durban. Group pricing is negotiable, so email us at info@rehtraining.co.za with your team size and location for a quote.

name: Fall Protection Planning
description: This course gives supervisors, safety officers and site managers the practical skills to plan fall protection for work at height. It covers identifying fall hazards, assessing the risks of working at height, choosing the right prevention and arrest measures, and preparing a workable fall protection plan for the site. Learners finish with a clear process they can apply to their own workplaces, from selecting anchor points to planning what happens in an emergency. The course runs over one day and suits anyone responsible for planning safe height work.
outcomes: Identify fall hazards and assess the risks of work at height
Select appropriate fall prevention and fall arrest measures for a task
Prepare a fall protection plan that covers anchor points, equipment and procedures
Plan for emergency response and rescue during height work
Apply the plan to a workplace and review it as conditions change
audience: Safety officers and site managers who plan height work
Supervisors responsible for teams working at height
Construction and maintenance managers preparing site procedures
Employees who write or update fall protection plans for their employer

faqs.q: How much does the Fall Protection Planning course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R700 per person and runs for one day. Group bookings are negotiable, so ask for a quote when you book a team. Daily classes run at our Midrand and Durban centres, and we can present the course on site at your premises. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za to book.

faqs.q: What is a fall protection plan?
faqs.a: A fall protection plan sets out how work at height will be done safely on a site. It identifies the fall hazards, states which prevention or arrest measures will be used, and covers anchor points, equipment and rescue arrangements. This course shows you how to prepare one and keep it up to date.

faqs.q: Who should do this course?
faqs.a: It is aimed at people who plan or supervise height work, such as safety officers, supervisors and site managers. You do not need to be an engineer. The course is practical and works through the steps of assessing a worksite and preparing a plan your team can follow. It is a one day course priced at R700 per person.

faqs.q: Is this course different from Fall Protection Plan Developer?
faqs.a: Yes. Fall Protection Planning gives you the working knowledge to assess height work and prepare a plan. The Fall Protection Plan Developer course covers the formal SAQA aligned unit standard for assessing a worksite and preparing a fall protection plan. Email us at info@rehtraining.co.za if you are not sure which one your employer requires.

If you are unsure whether your certificate is current, send it to us via email at info@rehtraining.co.za and we will check.

You also learn to complete tagging records and recommend corrective actions. Practical inspection exercises happen on the day.

faqs.a: It helps to be familiar with scaffolding, because the course moves quickly through inspection criteria for different systems. If you are new to scaffolding, do the Scaffolding Erector course first. Inspectors are usually people who already work around scaffolds and need the formal inspection skills. You can book either course via email at info@rehtraining.co.za, and classes run daily.

faqs.q: How long is the certificate valid?
